name: Wide arpeggiated wave
description: the nocturne engine. One bass note, then the chord unfolding upward across an octave and a half: `Ab1e Eb3e Ab3e C4e Eb4e C4e Ab3e Eb3e`. The span from the bass to the top of the figure is 15–20 semitones; the *width* is the sound.
shorthand: Ab1e Eb3e Ab3e C4e Eb4e C4e Ab3e Eb3e

name: Bass note plus displaced chord
description: `Bb1q [F3,Bb3,D4]q [F3,Bb3,D4]q` in 3/4. The mazurka and waltz shape. The gap between the bass and the chord is the point; closing it makes it sound like a folk band.

name: Rocking tenths
description: `Ab1e C3e Ab1e C3e …`. A tenth apart, alternating. Warm and open, and the tenth is what makes it Romantic rather than an octave.

name: Sustained pedal bass under moving inner voices
description: `Ab1w // Eb3e F3e Gb3e F3e Eb3e F3e Gb3e F3e`. The bass holds for the whole bar while a middle voice moves. This is genuine two-voice left-hand writing and it is what most generated Chopin is missing.
shorthand: Ab1w // Eb3e F3e Gb3e F3e Eb3e F3e Gb3e F3e

name: Chromatic inner-voice descent
description: the bass stays, the note above it falls by semitone across four bars: `C3 → B2 → Bb2 → A2`. Chopin's most reliable way of making a repeated harmony feel like it is going somewhere.

name: Doubled octaves in the bass
description: `[Ab1,Ab2]h [Eb2,Eb3]h`. For weight at a climax, or for the ballades' declamatory passages. Rare and heavy; do not use it as a default.

name: Waltz oom-pah-pah, widely spaced
description: `Ab1q [C3,Eb3]q [C3,Eb3]q`. The textbook figure, but the bass is an octave lower than a Classical waltz would put it and the chord is thinner (two notes, not three).

name: Free arpeggio spanning the whole hand
description: `Db1e Ab1e F2e Ab2e Db3e F3e Ab3e Db4e`, a two-and-a-half-octave sweep in one bar. The barcarolle and the later nocturnes. Written as one gesture, pedalled through.
shorthand: Db1e Ab1e F2e Ab2e Db3e F3e Ab3e Db4e

name: Repeated chord with a moving bass
description: the chord stays put while the bass walks underneath it: `Ab1e [C3,Eb3]e G1e [C3,Eb3]e F1e [C3,Eb3]e …`. Motion without any change in colour.

name: The left hand carries the melody
description: in the middle register, with the right hand accompanying above. Used for a return, or for the middle section of a nocturne. The tune sounds completely different an octave lower with a different attack, which is the reason to do it.

name: Silence under a cadenza
description: `rest_w`. The right hand runs free and the left hand simply stops. Chopin does this at every written-out ornamental flourish; keeping the accompaniment going through one is the surest way to make it sound mechanical.

name: Repeated chords, steady and unhurried
description: `[C3,E3,G3]e ×8` or in triplets, `[C3,E3,G3]trip_e ×6` per bar in 2/4. The *lied* accompaniment, and the single most Schubertian sound. It can run for sixteen bars unchanged; that is the point, not a defect.

name: Walking bass in octaves
description: `[C2,C3]q [G2,G3]q [C2,C3]q [G2,G3]q`. Patient, trudging, the "wanderer" tread. Slow and even.

name: Triplet accompaniment against duple melody
description: `[C3,E3]trip_e ×6` under a melody in eighths and quarters. The cross-rhythm is gentle and constant, and it is everywhere in the late works.

name: Broken chord rising and falling within an octave
description: `C3e E3e G3e E3e C3e E3e G3e E3e`. Narrower than Chopin's arpeggios, and closer in feel to Alberti than to a Romantic wave.
shorthand: C3e E3e G3e E3e C3e E3e G3e E3e

name: Bass alone on the downbeat, chord sustained above
description: `C2q [E3,G3]h.` in 4/4. Spacious, and it leaves room for a long melodic line.

name: The dactyl rhythm
description: long-short-short, `C3q C3e C3e`, repeated for pages. The "Death and the Maiden" figure. Obsessive and hypnotic.

name: Tremolo, quiet
description: `[C3,E3]s ×16` at `pp`. Not a Beethoven storm; a shiver. Used under a sustained melody at a moment of harmonic strangeness.

name: Held chord across the bar
description: `[C3,E3,G3]w~`. Schubert lets harmonies sit. Where a Classical composer would move on, he stays, and the stillness is the expression.

name: Octave doubling of the melody in the bass
description: for a return, or for the second verse of a strophic form. Same tune, entirely different weight.

name: Bass drops out under a modulation
description: the accompaniment thins to two upper notes while the harmony slides somewhere remote, then the bass returns on the new key. His most reliable way of making a distant modulation sound inevitable.

name: Off-beat chords with an empty downbeat
description: `rest_e [C3,E3,G3]e [C3,E3,G3]e [C3,E3,G3]e`. The bar has no floor under beat 1. His most recognisable texture.

name: Syncopated bass
description: the bass note tied over from the previous bar, so it is never struck on the downbeat.

name: Broken chord spanning a tenth
description: `C2e G2e E3e G2e`, warmer than an octave figure.

name: Inner-voice melody
description: the tune in the middle of the texture, played by the left hand's thumb, with accompaniment above and below.

name: Repeated chords, agitated
description: `[C3,E3,G3]s ×16` under a declamatory melody.

name: Contrapuntal bass
description: a real second line, from his Bach study.

name: Widely-spaced sustained chords
description: for the intimate slow pieces.

name: Dotted-rhythm march bass
description: `C2dq C2e G2dq G2e`, for the character pieces.

name: Arpeggio crossing above the right hand
description: hand crossing as colour.

name: Bare octaves
description: for a declamatory opening.

name: Silence for a beat mid-phrase
description: the texture stops and restarts.

name: Rolled tenths
description: `C2e E3e C2e E3e`. Brahms's hands were large and the tenth is his signature interval. Wider and warmer than an octave.

name: Broken chords in wide spacing
description: `F2e C3e Ab3e C4e F3e C3e`. Spanning two octaves, filling the middle register that Chopin leaves open.
shorthand: F2e C3e Ab3e C4e F3e C3e

name: Cross-rhythm against the melody
description: triplets in the left hand under duple in the right, or the reverse, sustained for whole phrases. Two against three is his normal state, not an effect.

name: Hemiola at cadences
description: the 3/4 regrouped as 3/2 across two bars approaching a close. So characteristic it is almost a fingerprint.

name: Chorale texture in the left hand
description: four real voices moving together in the lower register, drawn from his study of early music.

name: Sustained inner pedal
description: a held middle voice while the bass and melody move around it. Thickens without adding motion.

name: Arpeggio with the thumb carrying a countermelody
description: the top of the LH figure forms a second tune.

name: Syncopated accompaniment
description: the chord entering off the beat throughout a phrase, so the downbeat has no chord under it.

name: Bare octaves for a stark statement
description: usually at an opening or a return.

name: The wide-spanning broken chord
description: a tenth or more between the bass and the top of the figure, rolling in even values. The gesture Liszt inherited. `C2e G2e C3e E3e G3e E3e C3e G2e`
shorthand: C2e G2e C3e E3e G3e E3e C3e G2e

name: Rapid repeated chords
description: the same chord struck in even eighths or sixteenths under a melody, driving and orchestral.

name: The horn-fifths accompaniment
description: parallel thirds and sixths in the left hand imitating a horn pair. His signature, and the sound of *Der Freischütz*. `[C3,E3]q [B2,D3]q [C3,E3]h`

name: Offbeat chords over a marked bass
description: the waltz and the polonaise inheritance, 15% of the armed bars.

name: Long pedal point under a build
description: 12% of bars; used for the operatic crescendos.

name: Octave tremolo in the bass
description: for storm and supernatural scenes.

name: Three-octave arpeggio sweep
description: `Ab1e Eb2e Ab2e C3e Eb3e Ab3e C4e Eb4e`. One bar, one gesture, the full compass of the hand's reach with pedal. The signature sound.
shorthand: Ab1e Eb2e Ab2e C3e Eb3e Ab3e C4e Eb4e

name: Leaping bass
description: a low octave on the beat, a chord two octaves higher off it: `[Ab1,Ab2]q [Eb3,Ab3,C4]q [Ab1,Ab2]q [Eb3,Ab3,C4]q`. The distance is the effect; a close-position version of this is a waltz.

name: The "third hand"
description: the melody in the middle register, shared between the hands, with figuration above and below it. Written as a left-hand line that *is* the tune while the right hand ornaments around it.

name: Tremolo in the low register
description: `[Ab1,Eb2]s ×16`. Orchestral: it is a string tremolo transcribed. Under a sustained chordal melody it produces the "orchestra at the keyboard" texture the transcriptions are built on.

name: Repeated octaves, driving
description: `[Ab1,Ab2]e ×8` at `ff`. Relentless, and the basis of the bravura passages.

name: Chromatic scale in octaves
description: both hands, or the left alone, sweeping across two octaves. Transitional, and used to obliterate the previous key.

name: Bass alone, unaccompanied, declamatory
description: a single melodic line low on the instrument with nothing above it. Used at openings and before returns. Sparse and rhetorical.

name: Alternating hands on one figure
description: the two hands share a single arpeggio or scale, alternating notes, so it can run faster and wider than either could alone. A virtuoso device with a real textural result.

name: Harmonic pedal with chromatic inner motion
description: a held low octave while an inner voice slides chromatically. Liszt's tension-builder, usually before a climax.

name: Silence, complete
description: Liszt drops everything for a bar with a fermata, more often than any Romantic composer. The rhetoric is operatic: a pause before the next declamation.

name: Rippling broken chords
description: `C3e G3e E4e G3e C3e G3e E4e G3e`, even and light, in the middle register. The Song Without Words accompaniment.
shorthand: C3e G3e E4e G3e C3e G3e E4e G3e

name: Light staccato chords
description: `[C3,E3]e:stacc ×8` at `pp`. The scherzo idiom: fast, dry and even.

name: Oom-pah, transparent
description: bass and chord, but higher and lighter than a Classical version.

name: Arpeggio spanning an octave and a half
description: smooth and unhurried.

name: Sustained chorale chords
description: for the hymn-like slow movements and the religious works.

name: Repeated-note pulse
description: under a sustained melody.

name: Held pedal with light figuration above it.
description: Held pedal with light figuration above it.

name: Full sustained chords under a melody
description: `[C2,G2,C3,E3]h`. Rich, spread wide, the string-section sound.

name: Repeated chords, throbbing
description: `[C3,E3,G3]e ×8`, an insistent pulse under an intense melody.

name: Arpeggiated harp-like figure
description: even, wide, from the ballet textures.

name: Waltz oom-pah-pah, warm and full
description: bass then two full chords, not the thin Chopin version.

name: Descending chromatic bass
description: under a sustained melody — his standard intensifier.

name: Octave doubling of a melodic bass line
description: for weight.

name: Tremolo
description: under a sustained chordal melody, transcribing strings.

name: Pizzicato-style staccato bass
description: short, detached, from the ballet.

name: Counter-melody in the left hand
description: answering the right.

name: Pedal point under rising sequences
description: the standard build to a climax.

name: Bare unison octaves
description: for a fate-motif statement.

name: Alberti bass
when_to_use: Simple support (stay out of melody's way)

name: Murky bass (octave alternation)
when_to_use: Simple support (stay out of melody's way)

name: Waltz bass (3/4, L:1/8)
when_to_use: Simple support (stay out of melody's way)

name: Rachmaninoff wide-span
density_suggestion: Sixteenth notes throughout; Dense sixteenths or heavy chords; Maximum density or massive chords

name: Scalar fill ascending
density_suggestion: Sixteenth notes begin; Sixteenth notes throughout

name: Tremolo
density_suggestion: Dense sixteenths or heavy chords; Maximum density or massive chords

name: Chordal with passing tones
density_suggestion: Sixteenth notes; Sixteenth notes throughout; Dense sixteenths or heavy chords

name: Written-out ornamental flourish
description: a cadenza-like run of small notes over a held or absent accompaniment, notated in real values (often 32nds or a burst of irregular groupings). Placed at a phrase's peak or before a return. The left hand usually stops.

name: The ornamented return
description: a melody comes back decorated rather than plain. This is Chopin's principal variation technique: same notes, more of them, arriving in a different order around the same anchors.

name: Appoggiatura sigh
description: a dissonance on the beat resolving down by step, slurred: `(Ab5q G5q)`. The core expressive gesture, and it should recur.

name: Rubato against a steady bass
description: the melody written with values that do not align evenly with the accompaniment: a triplet against duple, a quintuplet over four, dotted rhythms over even ones.

name: Chromatic passing motion inside a diatonic line
description: the melody steps through notes outside the key on its way between chord tones. Colour without modulation.

name: Long-breathed line
description: a phrase of eight or more bars that does not cadence in the middle. The line arches once and lands once.

name: Melodic leap of a sixth or seventh, filled in on the way back
description: the operatic gesture: an expressive upward leap, then a stepwise descent from it.

name: Repeated note with changing harmony beneath
description: the melody holds one pitch while the chord under it moves, so the same note means something different in each bar.

name: The melody in the tenor
description: the tune moves to the left hand's upper register with accompaniment above and below it. Used for a middle section or a transformed return.

name: Chromatic voice leading
description: inner voices sliding by semitone between chords that would otherwise be plain. The harmony is often simple; the *motion* between chords is the interest.

name: Enharmonic pivot
description: a diminished seventh or an augmented sixth respelled to land in a remote key. Chopin modulates further and faster than any of his contemporaries.

name: Neapolitan and augmented-sixth colour
description: at moments of pathos, especially in the mazurkas and nocturnes.

name: Modal inflection from Polish folk music
description: a raised fourth (Lydian) or a flattened seventh in the mazurkas, and drone fifths in the bass. This is what separates a mazurka from a waltz.

name: A dominant that refuses to resolve
description: the chord held, decorated, delayed over several bars before the tonic finally arrives.

name: Parallel diminished sevenths descending
description: a sequence of the same chord shape sliding down by semitone or minor third. Transitional, and it dissolves the key.

name: Ternary with an ornamented return
description: A, contrasting B, then A again with the melody decorated. The nocturne and mazurka default.

name: The coda that dissolves
description: the texture thins, the register rises or falls away, the dynamic drops to `pp` or `ppp`. Chopin rarely ends loudly.

name: Mazurka rhythm
description: the stress on beat 2 or 3 rather than 1, in 3/4. Written as a dotted or accented second beat. Without it a mazurka is a waltz.

name: Rhythmic dissolution before a return
description: the pulse becomes ambiguous through irregular groupings, then the return re-establishes it.

name: Bel canto phrasing marks
description: long slurs over whole phrases, not bar by bar. A slur that stops at the barline is not this idiom.

section: Harmonic devices — the heart of the style
name: Major–minor inflection
description: the same melody, the same bass, one note changed from major to minor and back. Often on a repeat of a phrase just heard. His single most characteristic gesture and it costs one accidental.

section: Harmonic devices — the heart of the style
name: The flat submediant (♭VI)
description: arriving unprepared. C major side-stepping to A-flat major. No pivot, no preparation; the shift itself is the event.

section: Harmonic devices — the heart of the style
name: Chromatic mediant relations
description: keys a third apart with no common dominant: E major from C major, E-flat from G. Schubert modulates by colour rather than by function.

section: Harmonic devices — the heart of the style
name: The common-tone modulation
description: one note held while everything else moves into a remote key. The held note makes the impossible sound inevitable.

section: Harmonic devices — the heart of the style
name: Prolonged harmony
description: a single chord held for two, four, eight bars while the accompaniment figure continues. Stillness as expression.

section: Harmonic devices — the heart of the style
name: The augmented sixth as a door
description: used to leave a key sideways rather than to approach a dominant.

section: Harmonic devices — the heart of the style
name: Modal mixture throughout
description: borrowing freely from the parallel minor in a major-key piece (♭III, ♭VI, iv). Not a moment of darkness but a constant colour.

section: Harmonic devices — the heart of the style
name: A dominant that resolves somewhere unexpected
description: set up conventionally, then the resolution goes to a chromatic chord instead.

name: The long line
description: a melody of eight to sixteen bars with no interior cadence. Do not break it into two-bar units.

name: Repeated note as an anchor
description: the melody returns to one pitch again and again while the harmony beneath changes its meaning. Deeply his.

name: The sigh figure
description: a falling second, slurred, often repeated in sequence.

name: Melody doubled at the octave or the sixth
description: for a strophe's return.

name: Ornamental turn on a long note
description: a decorated arrival, vocal in origin.

name: The vocal cadence
description: the melody falls to the tonic by step from above, unhurried, with the accompaniment continuing under it.

name: Strophic variation
description: the same music repeated with a changed accompaniment, a changed mode, or a changed register. Schubert varies by *colour*, not by development. This is the alternative to Beethovenian argument.

name: The three-key exposition
description: a sonata exposition visiting a third key before settling, instead of moving straight to the dominant.

name: The long lyrical second subject
description: often the emotional centre of the movement rather than a foil to the first.

name: The coda that lingers
description: the material recalled quietly rather than summarised loudly.

name: Trudging accompaniment as a whole-piece character
description: one figure maintained for a movement, establishing a walking, wandering quality. The *Winterreise* manner, and it works in instrumental music too.

name: A silence before a modulation
description: a rest, then the music resumes in a distant key with no preparation.

name: Persistent syncopation
description: the melody or the accompaniment consistently off the beat for a whole piece.

name: Empty downbeat
description: beat 1 with nothing on it, repeatedly.

name: Metric ambiguity
description: the notated metre and the heard metre disagreeing for long stretches.

name: Dotted march rhythm
description: as a character marker.

name: Cross-rhythm between the hands.
description: Cross-rhythm between the hands.

name: The motto cipher
description: a short pitch sequence used as a signature and woven through a cycle (ASCH, or a name spelled in notes).

name: Inner-voice melody
description: the tune buried in the middle of the texture.

name: Fragmented, aphoristic phrases
description: a piece can be sixteen bars long and complete.

name: The sighing appoggiatura
description: densely used.

name: Melody in dialogue between the hands
description: a phrase begun by one and finished by the other.

name: Chromatic inner voices
description: over a static bass.

name: Deceptive resolutions
description: used repeatedly so the tonic is delayed.

name: Modal mixture
description: for sudden shadow.

name: Sequences of dominant sevenths
description: sliding chromatically.

name: Ending on an unresolved or ambiguous harmony
description: several of the character pieces simply stop.

name: The cycle
description: eight to twenty short pieces, each characterised, unified by a motto or a key scheme.

name: Contrasting alter egos
description: two opposed characters (impetuous / dreamy) alternating across a set. Florestan and Eusebius.

name: Quotation
description: a phrase from another work or another movement appearing briefly.

name: The unexpected ending
description: a piece that stops mid-gesture.

name: Literary titles and programmes
description: driving the character of each piece.

name: Hemiola
description: 3/4 heard as 3/2 across two bars, especially before a cadence. The single most Brahmsian rhythmic gesture.

name: Two against three
description: duple in one hand, triple in the other, sustained.

name: Syncopation across the barline
description: the melody entering off the beat and tied over, so the metre is felt rather than heard.

name: Metric displacement
description: the same figure re-entered a beat later than expected, holding the displacement for several bars.

name: Rhythmic augmentation of a motif
description: within the same passage.

name: Developing variation
description: each restatement of a motif differs: an interval widened, a rhythm dotted, a note added. Never a literal repeat.

name: Motivic saturation
description: every voice derived from the same cell, including the accompaniment.

name: Melody built from thirds and sixths
description: the intervals themselves are the signature sound.

name: Long-breathed line over a shorter harmonic rhythm.
description: Long-breathed line over a shorter harmonic rhythm.

name: The falling third as a motto
description: three descending notes, used to open and to unify.

name: Third-related key areas
description: rather than dominant ones.

name: Suspension and appoggiatura on nearly every strong beat
description: the harmonic surface is dense with prepared dissonance.

name: Pedal point with chromatic movement above
description: for a long build.

name: Plagal inflection at the end
description: the final cadence coloured by the subdominant.

name: Chromatic inner-voice motion
description: while the outer voices hold.

name: Sonata form with a developing exposition
description: development begins before the exposition ends.

name: Variation form as a whole movement
description: a ground bass or a passacaglia.

name: Cyclic return of a motif across movements.
description: Cyclic return of a motif across movements.

name: The quiet ending
description: dissolving rather than concluding loudly.

name: Archaism
description: a chorale, a canon, a passacaglia embedded in Romantic harmony.

name: The reminiscence motif
description: a theme attached to a character or an idea, returning transformed when that idea returns. Wagner's leitmotif in embryo.

name: The slow, dark introduction
description: before a fast movement — diminished harmony, low register, tremolo, resolving into the main allegro.

name: The storm scene
description: chromatic scales, diminished sevenths, tremolo, sforzandi. The Wolf's Glen is the model for a century of them.

name: The horn call
description: an open fifth-and-third fanfare in the natural-horn register, standing for the forest. His single most identifiable gesture.

name: Sudden dynamic and textural contrast
description: for theatrical effect: full texture to bare octaves in one bar.

name: The diminished seventh as the engine of drama
description: used for suspense, for modulation, and for the supernatural. He leans on it far harder than Beethoven.

name: Applied dominants everywhere
description: `V7/IV` is among the commonest harmonies in the armed corpus.

name: Chromatic mediant shifts
description: for a change of scene.

name: Enharmonic reinterpretation
description: of a diminished seventh to jump keys instantly.

name: Long dominant preparation
description: before an aria or a theme's return.

name: The wide singing leap
description: a sixth or an octave upward into a sustained note, vocal in origin.

name: Arpeggiated melody outlining the triad
description: the horn and clarinet inheritance, so the tune often moves by chord tones rather than by step.

name: Dotted rhythms in march and polonaise character.
description: Dotted rhythms in march and polonaise character.

name: The brilliant closing flourish
description: a rapid scale or arpeggio to end a section, written out.

name: The concert piece in linked sections
description: (Konzertstück) rather than separate movements — a form he effectively created.

name: The dance movement as a character piece
description: most famously the waltz treated as concert music.

name: Thematic transformation
description: the same interval sequence, new character. Slow and sustained, then fast and martial, then decorated and lyrical. Change everything except the intervals.

name: The theme in a new register
description: the identical material two octaves up or down is a different piece of music at the keyboard.

name: Rhythmic augmentation into a peroration
description: the theme in double values, fortissimo, in octaves, at the end.

name: Fragmentation into figuration
description: the theme's head becomes the basis of a run or a tremolo, so the virtuosity is thematic rather than decorative.

name: Octave passages
description: the melody in octaves in one or both hands, at speed. The bravura default.

name: The "third hand"
description: the melody in the middle register with figuration above *and* below it, shared between the hands.

name: Alternating hands on one line
description: a single scale or arpeggio split between the hands so it can run faster and wider than either could alone.

name: Orchestral tremolo
description: a low tremolo under a sustained chordal melody, transcribing a string section.

name: Cadenza
description: an unmeasured or freely-measured flourish, often over a held harmony, placed before a return or a final statement.

name: Repeated-note virtuosity
description: the same pitch struck rapidly with alternating fingers, a device borrowed from Paganini.

name: Wide leaps as gesture
description: the hand jumping two or three octaves between beats, the leap itself being the effect.

name: Chordal recitative
description: a declamatory passage in unison or in bare octaves, freely timed, between sections.

name: Chromatic third relations
description: keys and chords a third apart, with no functional connection. Liszt uses these more freely than anyone before him.

name: The augmented triad
description: as a colour and as a pivot. Symmetrical, so it belongs to no key, and it is his favourite way of dissolving one.

name: Diminished-seventh sequences
description: the same shape sliding by minor thirds, obliterating tonality for a passage.

name: Whole-tone and other symmetrical scales
description: especially in the late works, used as transitional colour.

name: Bare open fifths
description: for archaism, for the religious works, and for emptiness.

name: Unresolved dissonance at a section's end
description: the late works simply stop on an unresolved chord.

name: Modal harmony from Hungarian sources
description: the augmented second, the "Gypsy" scale, and drone accompaniment in the rhapsodies.

name: Double-function form
description: one movement that is simultaneously a sonata and a four-movement cycle. Ambitious; only relevant for a long piece.

name: The slow introduction that becomes the main theme
description: material introduced ambiguously and then revealed.

name: The apotheosis
description: the theme returning at the end transformed into a triumphal or hymnic version, at the loudest and widest point of the piece.

name: Episodic construction with a returning idea
description: the sections contrast strongly and the theme is what unifies them.

name: The song without words
description: an unbroken vocal melody over a rippling accompaniment, in a clear ternary shape.

name: Long-breathed lyrical line
description: with a single arch.

name: Melody in thirds and sixths
description: for warmth.

name: The fairy scherzo idiom
description: rapid, light, staccato, high, `pp`, in even note values. His invention and unmistakable.

name: Ornamental turn on an arrival note.
description: Ornamental turn on an arrival note.

name: Melodic sequence rising to a peak.
description: Melodic sequence rising to a peak.

name: Diatonic clarity
description: the harmony is simpler than his contemporaries', and the effect is transparency.

name: Chromatic passing motion inside a diatonic frame.
description: Chromatic passing motion inside a diatonic frame.

name: Modal mixture for a shadow
description: used sparingly and therefore effectively.

name: The plagal, hymn-like cadence
description: in the sacred and slow movements.

name: Sequence through closely related keys.
description: Sequence through closely related keys.

name: Strict ternary (ABA) with a varied return.
description: Strict ternary (ABA) with a varied return.

name: Sonata form, Classically proportioned
description: no expanded development, no disruptive coda.

name: Scherzo and trio
description: the scherzo fast and light, the trio contrasting in texture rather than in tempo.
